result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes basic infrastructure such as sidewalks and marked crosswalks, but is compromised by the presence of embedded trolley tracks and degraded pavement. A large portion of the right-hand side is obscured, limiting the assessment of potential signals or additional hazards in that area.

hazards.name: Embedded trolley tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks in the roadway create uneven surfaces and can be slippery or catch wheels/heels.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the foreground

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and potholes near the tracks and crosswalk area increase trip risks.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface around the tracks and intersection

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint crosswalks with high-visibility 'continental' patterns to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Roadway and Track Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair the asphalt around the trolley tracks to eliminate tripping hazards and uneven surfaces.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Yield to Pedestrian' signs to reinforce the right-of-way at the marked crossing.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely obstructed by active construction that completely blocks the sidewalk with fencing and heavy machinery. No temporary pedestrian bypass or crossing infrastructure is visible, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction fencing and a cherry picker completely block the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and middle ground along the building frontage

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Pedestrian Path
hazards.description: No temporary walkway is provided to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic during construction.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway edge adjacent to the construction site

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Bypass
interventions.description: Establish a protected, ADA-compliant temporary walkway in the roadway using water-filled or concrete barriers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Wayfinding Signage
interventions.description: Install signs directing pedestrians to safe crossing points or alternative routes around the construction zone.

interventions.title: Temporary Crosswalk
interventions.description: Mark a temporary crosswalk to allow pedestrians to safely reach the opposite sidewalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly degraded by active construction on the left side, which obstructs the sidewalk with fencing and barriers. There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals visible, and the presence of trolley tracks in the roadway adds a tripping hazard.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction fencing and orange water-filled barriers completely block the sidewalk on the left side of the image.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible roadway

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Path
interventions.description: Provide a safe, ADA-compliant temporary walkway around the construction site with proper shielding from traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks at intersections or mid-block locations to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps at all potential crossing points.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features basic infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but it lacks modern safety enhancements. The area is characterized by industrial-style buildings with zero setbacks, creating blind corners and a lack of physical buffers between pedestrians and the roadway.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center right, across the side street intersection

hazards.name: Blind Corner
hazards.description: The brick building is situated at the property line, creating a sharp visual obstruction for both pedestrians and drivers at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center left, where the brick building meets the side street

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement and Puddles
hazards.description: Cracked asphalt and standing water near the curb create potential trip hazards and slip risks for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and gutter area near the crosswalk

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines by 'daylighting' the intersection.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Add street trees or planters to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while improving the aesthetic environment.
